7 Mistakes New Linux Users Make - Datamation

1. Choosing the Wrong Linux Distribution

I have issues with that.As a Windows user never used Linux before, I have absolutely no idea what to look for. And the last thing you want is to try fiddling with 10 different Linux versions. As a Windows user trying Linux, I have no interest in discovering or fine tuning my Linux, I want an OS that I click install and it works. As a Windows user I am focused on productivity and tampering with Linux is not productivity.

the last thing you want is to try fiddling with 10 different Linux versions

Speak for yourself. I loved tinkering with more than 10 different Linux versions when I was a newb, coming over for the first time, trying to figure out what distro I would settle on.

Not everyone wants to be led around by the hand, presented with limited options, and told, that is the one you want.

Linux might not be the right OS for you. If you use Microsoft Office and don't want to switch to Libre Office, then honestly, don't even bother. There may be specific games or other software you use that are not easily available on Linux. So look that up first, and if that isn't the case and you think microsoft updates are annoying as fuck, you have everything to gain (a free OS for life) and nothing to lose. You should at least try out a live session, you don't even have to install anything, if you don't want to.

For former windows users, Linux Mint 18 Cinnamon 64-bit is probably the best choice because it has the same feel as windows 7. It's what I started out with and now, I'm on Arch Linux and never going back. If you can follow basic instructions and know how to search stuff, you don't understand, you will be fine. In you spare time, go grab an empty, USB stick, download the Mint ISO, extract it to the USB, reboot your PC, press F1 or escape to get into your BIOS, change your boot order to put the USB stick first, if you have UEFI BIOS, then turn off secure boot, save settings and exit, then try out the linux. And if you didn't understand my instructions, then search "how to try out a linux mint live session".

1. Assuming Software Updates Will Be Done For You

As a Windows user I expect that it is all point and click. When I started with Linux it was a hell because when I surfed the Internet I got conflicting solutions that was even time dependent. The solution from 2015 did not work anymore since something clanged.

A professional solution does not include typing in a huge command in a console. I just want to click on a button.

Linux Mint came very close to what I wanted. But the Install was still confusing. I almost gave up.

Installing software on mint is still confusing for me, as is updating. Installing the OS on a clean hard drive wasn't bad. Trying to update flash player so I can watch Hulu... Fucking impossible for me.

Windows is just the same, it isn't just a Linux thing. A solution to a problem from XP will not be the same in Windows 7, 8.1, 10 etc...

Let's not pretend that fixes for a Windows system are in any way less time dependant. Software moves on and changes all the time.
